stem: According to the Weigert-Meyer Law in a complete Duplex Collecting System, what are the typical anatomical insertions and clinical complications of the Upper Pole and Lower Pole ureters?

options.text: Upper pole ureter inserts medially/inferiorly with Ureterocele/Obstruction; Lower pole ureter inserts laterally/superiorly with Vesicoureteral Reflux (VUR)
Upper pole ureter inserts laterally with VUR; Lower pole ureter inserts medially with Ureterocele
Upper pole ureter has a short submucosal tunnel; Lower pole ureter is prone to ectopic ligation
Both ureters insert into a single orifice with equal obstruction risk

stem: A 2-year-old girl evaluated for febrile urinary tract infection undergoes Voiding Cystourethrogram (VCUG), which demonstrates reflux of contrast into a moderately dilated ureter and renal pelvis with blunting of the renal calyces. How is this Vesicoureteral Reflux (VUR) graded?

options.text: Grade I
Grade III
Grade II
Grade V

stem: Which of the following is considered an indication for continuous prophylactic antibiotic therapy (CAP) or surgical intervention in children with Vesicoureteral Reflux (VUR)?

options.text: Asymptomatic Grade I VUR in a 6-year-old child
Isolated non-febrile cystitis in an adult female
Recurrent febrile Urinary Tract Infections (fUTIs) despite observation or high-grade VUR (Grade IV-V) with breakthrough infections
Normal renal ultrasound without reflux on VCUG

stem: What is the initial immediate management step for a male infant diagnosed with Posterior Urethral Valves (PUV) presenting with acute urinary retention and electrolyte derangements?

options.text: Immediate Urinary Decompression using a feeding tube or transurethral catheter, alongside electrolyte stabilization
Emergency open transabdominal valve resection
High-dose intravenous Furosemide administration
Immediate bilateral nephrectomy

stem: A young adult with a history of unilateral renal agenesis and congenital solitary functioning kidney is evaluated for routine checkup. Urinalysis shows trace proteinuria and GFR is 65 mL/min/1.73m2. What is the primary pathophysiological driver of long-term CKD progression in a single functioning kidney?

options.text: Compensatory Glomerular Hyperfiltration leading to intraglomerular hypertension and secondary FSGS
Immune complex deposition in the subendothelial space
Amyloid fibril accumulation in the interstitium
Recurrent IgA vasculitis
